title: Seattle request #2106 command and enforcement timeline depth 1
summary: Primary Seattle records establish a time-bounded command layer around 12th & Jackson and North Beacon Hill without establishing corruption or improper political motive. Shon Barnes was chief during the June 17 enforcement expansion; Andre Sayles became interim chief July 30. Robert Brown had already moved from West Precinct command into Patrol Operations and was promoted to assistant chief in May 2026, while Heidi Tuttle remained South Precinct captain. A March 20 West Patrol emphasis at 12th & Jackson also shows proactive enforcement there before the June mayoral policy announcement.

No reviewed primary record establishes corruption, selective enforcement, improper political influence or political motive by a named employee in this fact pattern.

methods: primary Seattle command and policy-source review

data.question: Which public SPD command roles and operational layers can be tied to the #2105/#2106 locations and June 2026 enforcement policy without back-projecting current titles or inferring misconduct?
data.method: Reconciled dated mayoral and SPD releases with current command biographies, precinct geography, OIG publication inventory and a pre-policy 12th & Jackson patrol record.
data.framework: Current title, historical title, geographic responsibility, policy announcement, operational tasking, misconduct finding and political motive are separate predicates requiring separate evidence.
data.scope: Seattle Police command timeline, 12th & Jackson / Chinatown-ID, North Beacon Hill, Patrol Operations, RTCC and unresolved operational decision authority.
findings: Mayor Katie Wilson's June 17, 2026 statement announced expanded police personnel and a new enforcement posture at 12th & Jackson and North Beacon Hill.
Shon Barnes remained Seattle Police Chief on June 17; the July 30 SPD announcement records his resignation and Andre Sayles's appointment as interim chief on that date.

Current SPD biography material says Robert Brown left West Precinct command for the Patrol Operations Bureau in August 2025 and was promoted to Assistant Chief in May 2026, so he should not be modeled as West Precinct commander for the June 17 policy launch.

Current SPD material places Brown over Patrol Operations and Heidi Tuttle as South Precinct captain; current precinct geography places Chinatown/International District under West Precinct and Beacon Hill under South Precinct.

A March 20 SPD blotter entry records West Patrol officers conducting proactive foot and vehicle patrols around 12th Avenue South / South Jackson Street to disrupt narcotics use and illegal vending, showing a documented enforcement emphasis before the June 17 mayoral announcement.

The March 19 mayoral RTCC statement says SPD's Real Time Crime Center covers parts of the Chinatown-ID through 12th & Jackson and uses civilian SPD operators, adding a surveillance-support layer distinct from patrol command.

The current OIG report index contains 2026 accountability work but the reviewed public index does not establish a 12th & Jackson-specific corruption, selective-enforcement or political-motive finding against Barnes, Sayles, Brown, Tuttle or another named employee.
conclusions: The June 17 command timeline must be anchored to Barnes as chief and Brown as Patrol Operations leadership, not to later or stale title snapshots.
The existence of a pre-June West Patrol enforcement emphasis weakens any simplistic claim that enforcement at 12th & Jackson began only with the June mayoral announcement.
The evidence supports a command-and-support graph but not an individual-corruption or political-motive conclusion.
recommendations: Recover June and July operation orders, deployment/tasking records, incident command plans and unit approvals for 12th & Jackson and North Beacon Hill.
Resolve the actual West Precinct command assignment and relevant watch/unit supervisors for the dated operations from primary personnel or tasking records rather than stale directory pages.
Join any OPA/OIG findings or public-record releases to named decisionmakers only when the case or document materially concerns the operation.
counterarguments: Geographic command responsibility does not prove participation in a specific enforcement decision.
A mayoral policy statement does not identify who approved each arrest, deployment or tactical choice.
Absence of a current OIG report title is not proof that no complaint or investigation exists.
limitations: No low-level employee was identified from video appearance alone.
No home addresses, family information or private contacts were collected.
No political contribution was treated as evidence of improper motive without a decision-linking record.
unresolved: Who approved and commanded the June 17 enforcement deployment below the mayor/chief level?
Which West and South Precinct units, watches, detectives, LEAD partners or RTCC operators were formally tasked?
Do OPA/OIG, public-record, overtime or deployment records identify misconduct, disparate treatment, pressure or exculpatory findings tied to the operation?

data.research_question: What can current primary records establish about the personnel and decision chain around the #2105/#2106 Seattle enforcement fact pattern without turning title proximity into misconduct attribution?
data.method: Built a time-bounded command and operational-support layer from dated Seattle mayoral/SPD sources, current command biographies and accountability indexes.
classification_rules: Current title is not historical title.
Geographic responsibility is not proof of participation in a specific decision.
Political or policy disagreement is not corruption.
A misconduct or political-motive label requires direct or strongly corroborated evidence linking the person, conduct and motive.

findings.finding: Shon Barnes, not Andre Sayles, was SPD chief when the June 17 enforcement expansion was announced.

Robert Brown had moved into Patrol Operations before June 2026 and was promoted to assistant chief in May, so stale West-Precinct commander listings should not be back-projected onto the June operation.
A March 20 West Patrol narcotics/illegal-vending emphasis at 12th & Jackson predates the June mayoral policy announcement.
Reviewed primary material supports command and geographic relationships but does not establish individual corruption or improper political motive.
